cards.card_text: Hallelujah!"
The song's last word is Hallelujah!
This psalm opens with praise: "Hallelujah!

He closes by blessing the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting, tells all the people to say amen, and ends right where he started: "Hallelujah!" Go ahead, baker, say it, because mine comes out a little muffled through the mustache but it COUNTS.
cards.verse_text: Let all the people say, “Amen!” Hallelujah!
cards.snippet: Let all the people say, “Amen!” Hallelujah!

cards.card_text: Psalm 111 opens with one word: "Hallelujah!" No warm-up, no clearing his throat, the writer comes in HOT.
He opened with Hallelujah, and he closes with praise too: "His praise endures forever!" Me?
This psalm opens with "Hallelujah!" and goes straight to praise from the very first word.
First word out of the gate: Hallelujah!
The last word is the same as the first: Hallelujah!
He closes the whole song with one word: “Hallelujah!”
He signs off with "Hallelujah!" and that's the WHOLE psalm.
This psalm kicks the door open with "Hallelujah!" and calls people to praise the name of the LORD.
Then comes Hallelujah number two.
cards.verse_text: Hallelujah, for the LORD is good; sing praises to His name, for it is lovely.
cards.snippet: Hallelujah, for the LORD is good; sing praises to His name, for it…

cards.card_text: And the psalm closes the same way it opened: "Hallelujah!"

This psalm opens with one big word: "Hallelujah!" Then the writer turns and talks to himself: "Praise the LORD, O my soul." Friend, that's a man giving his own soul a pep talk, and I RESPECT it, because some mornings my soul needs one before the first oven's even warm.
And the psalm signs off right where it started: "Hallelujah!" Same word at the front door and the back door, friend, so praise gets the first word AND the last word.
Friend, nobody signs this psalm, but it opens LOUD: "Hallelujah!" The writer says it's good to sing praises to our God, and pleasant and lovely to praise Him.
And the psalm ends right where it started: "Hallelujah!"
Psalm 148 opens with one word: "Hallelujah!" Then the psalm writer starts calling out, one after another, who should praise the LORD.
And the psalm ends right where it started: "Hallelujah!" He opened with it and closed with it, friend, with all of heaven and earth packed in between like a cookie box filled RIGHT up to the lid.
Psalm 149 opens with "Hallelujah!" and calls for a new song to the LORD.
Hallelujah!"
Psalm 150 is the very last psalm, and it opens with a call: "Hallelujah!
Hallelujah!" Friend, I'm a stamper on a gold base with no lungs at ALL, and you better believe I'm still waving this mustache.
They're shouting, "Hallelujah!
cards.verse_text: After this I heard a sound like the roar of a great multitude in heaven, shouting: “Hallelujah!
cards.snippet: …a sound like the roar of a great multitude in heaven, shouting: “Hallelujah!

cards.card_text: A second time they call out: "Hallelujah!
cards.verse_text: And a second time they called out: “Hallelujah!
cards.snippet: And a second time they called out: “Hallelujah!

cards.card_text: And all they say is "Amen, Hallelujah!" Friend, I have never said ANYTHING in two words in my whole life.
cards.verse_text: And the twenty-four elders and the four living creatures fell down and worshiped God who sits on the throne, saying: “Amen, Hallelujah!”
cards.snippet: …fell down and worshiped God who sits on the throne, saying: “Amen, Hallelujah!”

cards.card_text: These voices cry out Hallelujah too, and they give a reason.
cards.verse_text: And I heard a sound like the roar of a great multitude, like the rushing of many waters, and like a mighty rumbling of thunder, crying out: “Hallelujah!
cards.snippet: …of many waters, and like a mighty rumbling of thunder, crying out: “Hallelujah!
